intent: The drawn rail a progress indicator fills.
typical_uses: The track of a progress root, hosting its indicator

dont_use_when.situation: A short busy state of unknown duration, with no percentage to measure

mounted_in.note: The exported Progress wrapper always draws its own track, so a standalone ProgressTrack belongs under the primitive package's own Progress.Root.

invariants.text: A ProgressTrack reads the nearest progress root's state through React context and throws when there is none: it must sit inside a progress root, whichever package exports it.

The track carries its root's status as a data attribute - `data-indeterminate`, `data-progressing` or `data-complete` - and the stylesheet's indeterminate sweep selector keys on the track's own attribute, not the indicator's.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the track's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the track's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (status). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through progress.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A track hosting its indicator, beside the primitive's own root
good.code:
import { Progress as ProgressPrimitive } from '@base-ui/react/progress';

<ProgressPrimitive.Root value={42}>
  <ProgressTrack>
    <ProgressIndicator />
  </ProgressTrack>
</ProgressPrimitive.Root>

bad.title: A track nested inside the kit's Progress wrapper
bad.why: The wrapper renders its own track after the children and there is no prop to suppress it, so this draws two bars. Keep the wrapper's own track, or compose beside the primitive's own root.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ProgressTrackState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the track's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ProgressTrackState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the track's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (status). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through progress.module.css, not through this.
